Data & Platforms: IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics
Real-world time series datasets (Astronomy, EEG, Unemployment, Temperature, Chicago, Apple, Doge, Flights, Tourists)
Application Areas: Cognitive Bias Mitigation in Visual Analytics
Key Research Thinking Patterns: Dual-System Cognitive Bias Analysis: Applying dual-system theory to identify how System 1 processing drives practitioners to prioritize visual aesthetics over structural faithfulness in dimensionality reduction, validated through controlled user studies measuring exposure time and color encoding effects.

Perceptual Limit Quantification: Empirically determining the 'subitizing limit' in data visualization by measuring human performance stability across 2–15 categories in multi-class scatterplots, establishing that accuracy declines according to Fechner’s Law beyond six categories.

Distortion-Aware Interaction Design: Developing dynamic point relocation algorithms that correct projection-induced errors (missing/false neighbors) in multidimensional projections, enabling accurate cluster separation and interactive labeling in noisy geospatial datasets.

Visual Noise and Feature Preservation Modeling: Investigating human re-drawing behaviors in noisy time series to categorize strategies (Replicator, Trend Keeper, De-noiser), revealing that users semantically preserve trends and peaks while discarding periodicity and noise.
Summary Description: Ghulam Quadri specializes in Visual Analytics and Human-Computer Interaction, focusing on the intersection of cognitive psychology and data visualization. His research empirically investigates human perceptual limits, such as the subitizing threshold in categorical scatterplots, and cognitive biases like the preference for visual interestingness over structural faithfulness in dimensionality reduction. He develops novel interaction techniques, including Distortion-aware Brushing for multidimensional projections, to enhance cluster analysis reliability. Additionally, he evaluates temporal data visualization strategies, analyzing how visual noise influences feature preservation in time series. His work leverages extensive user studies, crowdsourced experiments, and real-world datasets to create human-centric, reliable visual analytics tools for high-dimensional and temporal data.
